_README: Goldened two-layer shim gap inventory. See test/shim-surface.test.cjs for what
this is and why it is a reviewed MAP rather than a must-be-empty gate.
Regenerate with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1, and add a note below for anything new.
Measured against the EXTRACTED cli.cjs (~21MB), never the 255MB Bun binary.

_notes.intl: NOT a node builtin — libexec/node-shim/modules/intl.cjs backs the Intl GLOBAL, not a require()able module, so neither side can enumerate it by name. Allowed, not a gap.
_notes.Bun.SQL: FIXED (no longer a layer1 gap, kept as history). Was an ACTIVE DIVERGENCE: upstream guards it with `if (typeof Bun > "u") throw Error("claude gateway requires the native binary")`, TRUE under real node ("undefined" > "u") but FALSE under quaude because bun-shim defines a Bun global at all — so the guard was defeated and `new Bun.SQL(...)` produced a bare `Bun.SQL is not a constructor` instead. bun-shim.cjs now gives Bun.SQL a throwing constructor that hands back upstream's own message verbatim. Reachability: confirmed NOT on the -p/interactive routes — Bun.SQL is used only inside the `claude gateway --config <path>` subcommand (a separate commander-registered enterprise auth/telemetry server), the sole call site in the bundle. See test/bun-shim-sql-guard.test.cjs.
_notes.Bun.WebView: BENIGN, and a good example of the shape we want: guarded by `"WebView" in Bun`, correctly false under the shim, so the branch is skipped and the function returns false. Feature detection that works. UNMEASURABLE, not merely unreached: CLODE_SHIM_PROBE (libexec/node-shim/internal/probe.cjs) wraps only node:* builtins loaded through loader.cjs's loadBuiltin() (its sole installProbe call site is loader.cjs:231) — libexec/bun-shim.cjs (the Bun.* global / bun: modules) has no probe instrumentation at all. This layer1 gap can never be armed by any corpus under the current probe design, so the BENIGN verdict above rests on code audit alone, not on measured reachability. See test/shim-surface/reachability.json's `probe_scope_limitation` and `unmeasurable` fields.
_notes.bun:jsc: BENIGN. One site: `try { let {heapStats} = await import("bun:jsc") ... } catch {}` for heap diagnostics. The rejection is caught, so a missing module degrades to no heap stats, matching any non-Bun host. UNMEASURABLE, not merely unreached: same probe-scope limitation as Bun.WebView above — libexec/bun-shim.cjs is not instrumented by CLODE_SHIM_PROBE, so this layer1 gap can never be armed by any corpus regardless of whether the bundle reaches it. See test/shim-surface/reachability.json's `probe_scope_limitation` and `unmeasurable` fields.
_notes.bun:sqlite: DRIFT, not a gap: bun-shim declares an interceptor for it in PROVIDES but bundle 2.1.218 never imports it. Harmless dead weight; listed so the declaration's drift stays visible instead of silently accumulating.
_notes.http.request / https.request / net.creat: DECLARED WALLS — the same ones test/node-shim-wall-tripwires.test.cjs alarms on, rediscovered here independently without being told they exist. That rediscovery is the main evidence this map works. They throw branded node-shim errors rather than failing silently. MEASURED (phase 2 Task 4, reachability.json dated 2026-08-04 against bundle 2.1.218): unarmed across all three corpora that ran (apicheck, agentic, interactive) — see reachability.json's `unarmed` list. This is corpus coverage, not a clean negative: per reachability.json's `corpus_blind_spots`, agentic runs against a MOCKED Anthropic server so it structurally cannot exercise real TLS/HTTP client paths; apicheck's credentialed branch hung (RECIPE.md G6, see the crypto.* note below) before reaching whatever lies past it; interactive captures only a 10s no-keystroke initial paint (no typed turn, no tool use).
_notes.crypto.*: The largest cluster (X509Certificate, createPrivateKey/PublicKey, createSign/createVerify, sign, pbkdf2/pbkdf2Sync, KeyObject). MEASURED (phase 2 Task 4, reachability.json dated 2026-08-04 against bundle 2.1.218): unarmed across every corpus that ran (apicheck, agentic, interactive) — see reachability.json's `unarmed` list and `unarmed_meaning`. NAMED BLIND SPOT, not evidence of unreachability: the ONLY corpus that even attempts the credentialed branch — apicheck's -p items, seeded that run with a COPY of a real ~/.claude/.credentials.json, deleted immediately after — HUNG on the quaude side before completing a turn (naude: exit 0 both items; quaude: apicheck's own 60s timeout fired, status:143). This reproduces RECIPE.md G6 (previously believed darwin-ppc/Darwin-8-specific) on darwin-arm64 — see reachability.json's `apicheck` corpus entry (`note`, `perItem`). The crypto.* cluster is exactly where credentialed token-refresh / enterprise-auth (mTLS, Vertex/Bedrock) handling would live, so "unarmed" here means "we could not get far enough down the credentialed path to find out", NOT "the path does not use them". RECIPE.md G4 already flags that auth path as unverified. Phase-3's recommended next step (reachability.json's `phase3_recommendation`) is an isolated HOME seeded with a syntactically-valid FIXTURE credentials file — unrelated to any real account — to take the credentialed branch deliberately and safely, without hanging and without borrowing a real token.
_notes.fs.fchmodSync / fs.fstat / fs.ReadStream: FIXED (no longer layer2 gaps, kept as history). Were fd-flavored variants of things the shim DOES provide by path (chmodSync, statSync, createReadStream) — same class as the FileHandle.chmod gap that broke Edit, which is precisely why this map exists. fchmodSync now tracks fd->path at fs.openSync/close and chmods that path (no fd-based fchmod primitive in the sync-fs patch, same strategy FileHandle.chmod already used); fstat routes through the existing fstatSync via cbWrap; ReadStream is now a real class fs.createReadStream() constructs, not a lookalike. See test/node-shim-fs-fd-variants.test.cjs.
_notes.fs.watch: test/fidelity/RECIPE.md row C7 remains UNVERIFIED — nothing in this file or in reachability.json answers it; do not read the absence of an `fs.watch` entry anywhere in this measurement as a clean result. fs.watch is not a golden gap at all: it is a PRESENT property on the shim's fs, a never-firing stub (`fsMod.watch` in libexec/node-shim/modules/fs.cjs), verified `'watch' in fs === true` and `typeof fs.watch === 'function'`. CLODE_SHIM_PROBE fires ONLY on ABSENT properties (`!(prop in target)`, libexec/node-shim/internal/probe.cjs lines 39 and 45) — so an access to a PRESENT-but-stubbed API like this one structurally cannot arm the probe in either direction, and grepping reachability.json for "fs.watch" always comes back empty, proving nothing about reachability. This probe is structurally blind to PRESENT-BUT-STUBBED APIs generally, not just this one. Answering C7 needs a different instrument: a logging wrapper on the EXISTING stub recording whether any of its four known bundle call sites (jobStateNameSync, useBgSessionPr, an unref'd private-field watcher, vendored chokidar) ever arms a listener on the -p / interactive routes.
_notes.child_process.fork / ChildProcess: fork() has no meaning under tjs (no node child bootstrap). If a reachable path ever forks, that is a design question, not a missing function. MEASURED (phase 2 Task 4, reachability.json dated 2026-08-04 against bundle 2.1.218): unarmed across apicheck/agentic/interactive. Per reachability.json's `corpus_blind_spots`, agentic's four scripted flows (Bash, Edit, Workflow, subagent, MCP-ws) do not exercise child_process.fork by construction — a coverage gap in the corpus, not a confirmed absence in the bundle. Not probed on the credentialed apicheck path either (hung at G6, see crypto.* note above).
_notes.stream.Duplex: FIXED (no longer a layer2 gap, kept as history). Was reads-only (6), no calls — likely instanceof / prototype checks. Implemented as a real ES class in libexec/node-shim/modules/stream.cjs (phase 2 Task 5), modeled on the AWS SDK's ChecksumStream shape found verbatim in the extracted bundle. MEASURED armed: all three corpora that ran (apicheck, agentic, interactive) per reachability.json's `armed` map, `tracked_in_golden: true`.
_notes.v8.* / perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay: diagnostics and telemetry; absent means no stats, not broken behavior. MEASURED (phase 2 Task 4, reachability.json dated 2026-08-04 against bundle 2.1.218): unarmed across apicheck/agentic/interactive. Per reachability.json's `corpus_blind_spots`, the agentic corpus's four scripted flows don't exercise v8 heap stats or perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay by construction. Not probed on the credentialed apicheck path either (hung at G6, see crypto.* note above).
_notes.http.request / https.request: REMOVED from layer2 on 2026-08-22 because they are now IMPLEMENTED (libexec/node-shim/modules/http.cjs, client section; characterized in test/node-shim-http-client.test.cjs). Kept as history because WHY matters: this map listed them as gaps, and the companion wall-tripwire declared them latent, but neither could say whether upstream REACHED them. Measurement (instrumented shim + fused quaude + driven flows) said: not on the default Anthropic backend (axios picks its XHR adapter under tjs, because txiki defines a global XMLHttpRequest), but YES on Bedrock — 10 http.request calls at the EC2 instance metadata service from the AWS SDK credential chain, and an https.request at bedrock.<region>.amazonaws.com from @smithy/node-http-handler. That is the shape of evidence this map is meant to prompt, and it is why the entry is gone rather than annotated.
_notes.net.createServer / net.connect: STILL A GAP, and the reason npm `ws` cannot connect under quaude: ws's initAsClient unconditionally passes `createConnection` to http.request, so it never uses the shim client's own socket. The shim client refuses that option by name (ERR_SHIM_HTTP_UNSUPPORTED_OPTION) rather than ignoring it. Closing this means a real net.Socket, which is a bigger job than the HTTP client was.
_notes.SCANNER REBUILD 2026-08-29: The layer-2 list moved because the SCANNER was repaired, not because upstream suddenly reached for new APIs. From 2.1.243 upstream ships a code-split ESM graph and emits ZERO require() for builtins (measured: 0 aliases for fs, os, path, crypto, net, http, child_process, stream, util, tty, v8 - every module but worker_threads), so layer2Gaps `continue`d past every module and reported NO GAPS AT ALL. The 16 entries below were stale 2.1.218 measurements that survived only because the golden test asserts layer 1 first and died on Bun.ant before reaching layer 2. The companion canary ("the scanner still finds the known fs.watch call sites") went red and stayed red for weeks as a tolerated baseline; it was right, and it was the only thing standing between this map and silent uselessness. Repaired in three steps, all in shim-surface/bundle-refs.cjs: read graph.json sources (real strings) instead of the escape-laden graph runner; learn ESM's three binding shapes (import*as X / import X / import{prop as x}); and resolve bindings MODULE-SCOPED, because minified names are one character and a bundle-wide lookup made every `n.abort()` evidence for `process.abort` (10 such phantoms, now gone).
_notes.util.getSystemErrorName: FIXED 2026-08-29 (no longer a layer2 gap, kept as history). Two of the eight NEWLY VISIBLE entries above were triaged the day the repaired scanner surfaced them; this is the one that got implemented. Upstream's single import site is the dirSync anchor module (`import{getSystemErrorName as vn,promisify as gt}from"util"`), whose only call reads darwin's __error() through bun:ffi and renders `code: vn(-b)` when an *at() syscall fails. MEASURED reachability, correcting the triage that sent this task out: that call site is behind the bun:ffi WALL, not on the credentials-store path — libexec/bun-shim.cjs's `bun:ffi` provides a dlopen() that throws, upstream catches it inside Bn() and sets the anchor to null ("dirSync anchor: bun:ffi unavailable"), so vn is never called today. Implemented anyway, and the Bun.ant reasoning is exactly why the two decisions differ: nothing FEATURE-DETECTS getSystemErrorName, so providing it advertises no capability we cannot honor, and the alternative was the interop facade's lazy thrower firing at the precise moment an errno was being named. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, because the obvious one is wrong: node answers from LIBUV's error map, not from os.constants.errno, and on darwin/arm64 the two disagree on 18 of 79 names (EWOULDBLOCK must answer "EAGAIN"; EOPNOTSUPP/ECHILD/EDEADLK/... must answer "Unknown system error -N"). The shim asks the engine's own libuv via `new tjs.Error(n).code` (= uv_err_name), so no table is transcribed. Differential-locked against host node by test/node-shim-system-error-name.test.cjs.
_notes.zlib.createZstdDecompress: INTENTIONAL GAP, decided 2026-08-29, same shape as Bun.ant above and pinned by test/zlib-zstd-stream-gap.test.cjs. Upstream's single import site is the NATIVE release downloader (`import{createZstdDecompress as rt}from"zlib"` beside `var xe="https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases"`): it streams `${base}/${version}/${platform}/${file}.zst` through `pipeline(res.data, hashTap, rt(), sizeTap, fileStream)`. NOT the sync zstd clode already provides — that one is a HOST TOOL (libexec/host-provision.cjs + bun-graph.cjs shell out to zstd/unzstd/zstdcat at CARVE time, so a target never needs zstd to read upstream's embedded text assets). This is a streaming node:zlib Transform, and tjs has no native zlib at all (see libexec/node-shim/modules/zlib.cjs). MUST NOT BE STUBBED: upstream would then pipeline through a Transform that emits nothing or throws mid-download, turning "no zstd" into a corrupt or hung install; and unlike the sync path there is nothing to shell out to inside a pipeline. UNREACHABLE, for two INDEPENDENT reasons, both of which the pin asserts: (1) the downloader is only entered from the native updater / `claude update` install dispatch, and clode neutralizes all three updater widgets plus the manual dispatch; (2) upstream's installation type can only resolve to "native" inside `if(Al())`, and `Al()` is `typeof Bun<"u"&&Bun.isStandaloneExecutable===!0` — bun-shim reports that false, so QZ() returns "unknown" and the native widget is never mounted. If either wall falls, the gap becomes a live download failure and the decision must be re-taken.
_notes.NEWLY VISIBLE 2026-08-29 (os.devNull, fs: NOT new upstream behaviour and NOT yet reviewed - these are what the repaired scanner can see that the broken one could not. Each is a SINGLE import site (counts: os.devNull 2, the rest 1 apiece; fs.writev is one bare read), which is why the old require()-only scan missed them even before 2.1.243 went ESM. Recorded here so they are visible and diffable rather than absent; each still needs the same reachability question the crypto.* cluster got. Queued in BACKLOG.md.
_notes.child_process.fork: undefined REMOVED from the list 2026-08-29: with scoped resolution, 50 modules bind child_process and NONE reference .fork (0 named imports, 0 `<binding>.fork` sites). The 72 raw `fork(` substrings in the bundle are other objects' methods. Kept as history because the entry was true against 2.1.218.
_notes.Bun.ant: INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE, decided 2026-08-29 with the reasoning in libexec/bun-shim.cjs (beside spawnSync) and pinned by test/bun-shim-ant-gap.test.cjs. NEW in 2.1.243: Anthropic's own private Bun namespace, four syscall-backed methods — getPeerUid(fd)/getPeerPid(fd) (SO_PEERCRED / LOCAL_PEERCRED on a unix socket), setDumpable(bool) (Linux prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE,0)), memoryPressureLevel() (macOS). MUST STAY ABSENT, not stubbed: upstream gates a capability on `typeof Bun.ant?.getPeerPid === "function"`, so any stub — throwing or not — flips that probe true and advertises a peer-credential capability the shim cannot honor. That is the Bun.SQL trap in reverse. Absent is the faithful answer and the probe currently gets the RIGHT one. NOT IMPLEMENTED, checked rather than assumed: peer credentials are technically in reach (vendored txiki.js exposes socket_from_fd(fd) and sock.getopt() in mod_posix-socket.c), but BOTH call sites sit behind declared node-shim walls that throw first — net.connect for the UDS client, the missing net.Server for the daemon — so implementing them means implementing behind a closed door. setDumpable and memoryPressureLevel have no txiki primitive at all (prctl: zero hits in the source). OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR, and it is NOT uniformly graceful, which is why the walls are load-bearing rather than incidental: the capability probe degrades cleanly (upstream drops the capability); the macOS background low-memory probe degrades cleanly (lowMem reads false, so background sessions never retire early for memory pressure; non-macOS uses os.freemem() and is unaffected); Linux setDumpable reports "prctl unavailable" and the process stays dumpable, one hardening step short of upstream; but the daemon peer-uid check FAILS OPEN (catch -> null -> upstream reads "no objection"), and the UDS client peer-pid check REFUSES TO SEND outright ("endpoint-unverifiable"). Both of those are unreachable only because net.connect and net.Server throw first. test/bun-shim-ant-gap.test.cjs asserts both walls and goes RED the day either comes down, which is when this decision must be re-taken.
